text: Observed in the shared-expense-tracker pilot (e5dbe1f build): PlanReview round 3 returned scopeAssessment {kind: "challenges"} while every finding had category contradictory-artifacts or task-strategy-risks. plan-review.ts rejects that combination ("A challenges scope assessment requires an explicit scope challenge"), the failure is reported as PROVIDER_NATIVE_OUTPUT_INVALID with no diagnostic path, and the automatic semantic repair attempt (instruction return-complete-replacement-object, previous output echoed) produced the identical output and the identical failure fingerprint. The prompt already states the rule (provider-runner.ts: set kind challenges if and only if a finding has category missing-scope or missing-consumers), so this is provider non-compliance that the engine cannot recover from. Consider downgrading an unsupported challenges scope assessment into a disposition-able finding instead of failing the invocation, and surface the validation path in the failure.
